approved: Criminal Code Amendment (Inciting Illegal Disruptive Activities) Bill 2023
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create three new federal offences for inciting trespass, property damage or theft, and blocking traffic in major business districts and cultural centres.

A person would commit an offence by using a telecommunications service to send or publish material intended to incite another person to commit those crimes in a major business area, which is defined as a central business district or another precinct that serves as a hub for business or culture.

The maximum penalty is 12 months imprisonment for inciting trespass or traffic obstruction, and 5 years for inciting property damage or theft, and the bill would exempt journalists reporting in the public interest and people acting under whistleblower protections.
Introduce three new offences for inciting trespass, property damage or theft, and unlawful traffic obstruction in major business areas.
Define 'major business area' as a central business district or another precinct that is a centre of significant business or cultural activity.
Exempt journalists reporting in the public interest and whistleblowers protected by Commonwealth, state or territory law.
Set maximum penalties of 12 months imprisonment for inciting trespass and traffic obstruction, and 5 years for inciting property damage or theft.
Commence the whole Act the day after it receives Royal Assent.
People who use a carriage service to incite illegal disruptive activities in major business areas, and organisers who plan such activities online.
